subject: How to fix drawing order after merging 'long' data with fortify(sp)  in order to make facet_wrap of chloro maps

messages.author: 746a110d20a6f112
messages.subject: How to fix drawing order after merging 'long' data with fortify(sp)  in order to make facet_wrap of chloro maps
parts:
Hi-

I want to facet_wrap some cholorpleth maps. I have multiple
observations of the same value on the same polygon (ie- panel data).

I am using my own data read in with readShapeSpatial and converted
using fortifiySpatialPolygonsDataFrame

##Extract coordinate information from spData Frame, and merge with
data-------------------------------
rm(list=ls())
library(ggplot2)
library(gpclib)
library(maptools)
setwd('localpath')
load('ggplot2_geomPoly_PanelMap_quest.Rdata')


pdatM<-fortify.SpatialPolygonsDataFrame(datSpat)
pdatM2<-merge(pdatM,pdat,by.x='id',by.y='Dest')
#pdatM2<-pdatM2[order(pdatM2$order),] #I thought this would help but
it does not

pmap<-ggplot(pdatM2,aes(long,lat))+facet_wrap(~Org,ncol=2)
pmap<-pmap+geom_polygon(colour='white',aes(fill=value,group=group))
#also tried group=id
pmap #drawing order of polygons is messed up
#--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The problem (I think) is that the drawing order is messed up because
I'm merging with long data. I can make single maps just fine if I do
not have repeated observations, so I could concievably just make
multiple maps and then arrange them using grid functions, however I
would rather have the freedom/flexibility et cetera of doing it with
facet_wrap or facet_grid.

Any help would be appreciated. I will upload my .Rdata file to the
site.

Thanks

Frank
